analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only: changelog.d/startup-shape-warmup.md (added) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (a new paragraph at head lines 508-514). No executable code is in this batch, so no behavior was verified by reading source.

The documents describe a startup shape warmup that runs after model load and any self-test, before provider registration and before the local listener opens. It runs on the existing calibration session, idle gate and foreground lease, within the existing KV and service budgets. Its probes and cells publish no observations or work totals. Only its startup-preload pass skips the posture check. While a session runs, the periodic proactive MLX pool sweep waits; on-pressure reclaims still run. The warmup is disabled with DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP=0, and 'always' skips the probe.

Threat-model relevance: the warmup uses synthetic prompts, not consumer data. Consumer plaintext (A-001) is not touched, and nothing changes in the coordinator wire contract, attestation (TB-009, TB-011) or key custody. The prefix-cache threat T-041 is a possible interaction. The documents do not say whether warmup cells donate to or read from the SSD prefix cache, and they do not say whether the warmup uses a salt-scoped cache. The next pass should confirm that the warmup bypasses SSD donation and cannot create at-rest artifacts or cross-scope entries. The docs say the warmup publishes no work totals, which suggests it does not.

Availability considerations: the warmup adds up to 20 s per model before registration (T-029/T-057 style availability only). It is bounded, can be disabled by the operator and yields to requests.

The warmup code (probe, cache-donation behavior, deferral of the sweep) is not supplied. Those claims are unverified contract statements, not findings.
